verses.55:56: فِيهِنَّ قَٰصِرَٰتُ ٱلطَّرۡفِ لَمۡ يَطۡمِثۡهُنَّ إِنسࣱ قَبۡلَهُمۡ وَلَا جَآنࣱّ‏
verses.55:74: لَمۡ يَطۡمِثۡهُنَّ إِنسࣱ قَبۡلَهُمۡ وَلَا جَآنࣱّ‏

en_note: Manually curated for a Quranic root occurring exactly twice.
meaning: The root طَمَثَ (ṭamatha) denotes touching. Ibn Fāris gives its core simply as مس الشيء, citing al-Shaybānī that الطمث in Arabic speech is touch; it extends to the sense of deflowering and to menstruation.
meaning_source: Derived from the classical dictionaries (chiefly Maqayis al-Lugha, Ibn Faris d.1004) held in lexicon_full/
